test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2021: Official Paper (Held On : 9 June 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: With reference to the major regions of the northern plains, Bhabar is:

options.text: the older alluvium along the river beds forming terraces higher than the flood plain
a narrow belt of about 8 to 16 km that runs in the west-east direction along the foot of the Himalayas from the river Indus to Teesta
composed of newer alluvium and forms flood plains along the river banks
a broad long zone of northern India and southern Nepal running parallel to the lower ranges of the Himalayas

solution:
The correct answer is __**option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **After going down **from the **mountain **a **narrow belt **is formed which **is 8-16 km by the deposition **of **river pebbles**. This **belt **is called **Bhabar**. 
 
• It lies **parallel **to the **Shiwalik range**. **Streams again appear **in this **region **and **make it a wet **and **marshy region**.
 
• **The bhabar **tract comprises gravel and **un-assorted sediment deposits**.
 
• **This sediment present **in the **soil **is **deposited **by **rivers descending **from the **Himalayan mountains**.
 
• **This region **is not **good for cultivation**. **The area **is popular **with big trees with large roots**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhangar** - is the older alluvium along the river beds forming terraces, which are dark in colour, rich in humus content and productive. Bhangar is generally a well-drained and the most productive land of the Great Plains of India.
 
• **The Khadar** is composed of newer alluvium and forms the flood plains along the river banks. They are sandy clays and loams, drier and leached, less calcareous and carbonaceous.
 
• **Tarai,** also spelled Terai, region of northern India and southern Nepal running parallel to the lower ranges of the Himalayas.
